name: CortexDynamics Pulse SmartCarry BCI
description:
The CortexDynamics Pulse SmartCarry is a mid-range consumer BCI built around a fully integrated smartlink weapon interface, designed for legal civilian carry permit holders who want reliable neural weapon integration without paying military-grade prices. The implant provides a standard neural mesh platform — 1080p AR overlay, feed access, QUANTA payment integration, and 100 Mbps bandwidth — augmented by CortexDynamics' proprietary WeaponSync module, which establishes a direct neural handshake with compatible smartlink-enabled sidearms. When linked, the user receives real-time ballistic overlay data, round count, weapon status, and aim-assist projection directly into their AR field, with targeting data processed at the neural level for sub-20ms response integration. The WeaponSync module requires a valid Meridian 88 civilian carry permit to activate and is hardcoded to register and log all weapon draws with the city's Civic Arms Registry — a legal requirement for civilian smartlink BCIs.

The Pulse SmartCarry is the default choice for Tier 2-3 civilians who navigate Meridian's more dangerous districts and have obtained legal carry permits — a category that includes a significant portion of the working population in outer-ring neighborhoods, night-shift transit workers, small business owners in mixed-tier commercial zones, and off-duty security contractors. CortexDynamics markets the device aggressively in Shelf-adjacent Tier 2 districts with the tagline 'You carry the right — carry it smart,' and the implant has become a point of civic identity for communities where personal protection is a daily practical concern rather than a political statement. The mandatory civic arms logging feature is a persistent point of controversy, with some users viewing it as reasonable public safety infrastructure and others as an invasive surveillance mechanism that turns every weapon draw into a reportable event.
legality: Licensed — civilian carry permit required to activate WeaponSync module; base BCI functions unrestricted
installation_requirements: Outpatient procedure at CortexDynamics authorized clinic; carry permit verification required at installation for WeaponSync activation; local anesthetic; 2-hour procedure
rejection_risk: Low — standard mesh architecture with WeaponSync module housed in a passive state until permit verification; no increased rejection risk from weapon integration hardware
maintenance: Monthly automatic firmware updates including mandatory Civic Arms Registry compliance patches; semi-annual WeaponSync calibration at authorized clinic or CortexDynamics service kiosk; ballistic overlay recalibration recommended after every 500 rounds fired
specifications: {"bandwidth": "100 Mbps", "channels": 4, "ar_resolution": "1080p equivalent", "encryption": "AES-256 with government carry-compliance layer", "battery": "Passive induction with 8-hour active buffer", "latency": "12-18ms standard feed; 8ms WeaponSync channel", "weapon_sync_range": "2 meters passive; 0.3 meters active handshake", "compatible_weapons": "All Meridian 88 civic-certified smartlink sidearms", "arms_registry_logging": "Mandatory — all draws logged to Civic Arms Registry", "feed_protocols": ["CivNet", "MeshPublic", "QUANTA-Pay v4", "CivArms-Link v2"], "update_method": "OTA automatic; compliance patches cannot be deferred"}
side_effects: Weapon-context hypervigilance — some users report persistent low-level threat-scanning behavior as the WeaponSync module's environmental processing bleeds into general situational awareness
Ballistic overlay persistence — faint targeting reticle ghosting reported in peripheral vision during non-carry periods in approximately 12% of users
Mild motor cortex sensitization near the dominant hand during the first month of WeaponSync integration
Compliance patch installations occasionally cause 4-6 hour feed disruptions during major Civic Arms Registry system updates
cultural_context: In Meridian 88's outer Tier 2 districts, a Pulse SmartCarry is read as a statement of pragmatic self-reliance — the implant of someone who has assessed their environment honestly and made a legal, considered choice to be armed. In Tier 3 corporate environments, the same implant raises subtle unease, a reminder that the person across the table has internalized the infrastructure of lethal force. The mandatory civic arms logging remains a flashpoint: civil liberties advocates argue it creates a searchable database of every moment a citizen felt threatened enough to draw a weapon, while law enforcement consistently lobbies to expand registry access. A small but vocal community of Pulse users have discovered that certain grey-market firmware patches can introduce logging delays of up to 72 hours — technically still compliant, technically.

story_hooks: A series of weapon draws in a Tier 2 neighborhood are showing up in the Civic Arms Registry logged to the wrong users — someone has found a way to spoof WeaponSync identity signatures, and whoever is doing it is committing crimes that are being pinned on innocent carry permit holders.

A player character's Pulse SmartCarry receives a WeaponSync handshake from a weapon that isn't theirs — a ghost signal from a firearm that the Civic Arms Registry lists as destroyed three years ago, and which keeps appearing in the AR overlay whenever they enter a specific block.

CortexDynamics is quietly lobbying to expand the Civic Arms Registry logging to include not just draws but aim events — and a whistleblower needs help getting the draft legislation out before it passes in a closed corporate-municipal council session.
